scope: Read-only audit of command-dependent random draws and paired exogenous inputs. No worlds, models or provider calls were executed; no source files were edited.

findings.status: No direct source RNG contamination found
findings.detail: The episode string includes arm, seed and Date.now(), and is used for model scope, idempotency/request keys and run labels. It is not passed as the simulator seed or subsystem seed. Source draws use the configured seed plus subsystem/entity/event/index; there is no shared mutable PRNG or Math.random() in the physical engine/generators/contracts. Wall time is used by evaluation workers for deadlines, not by physical random draws.
findings.limit: This does not make different model runs deterministic. Different chosen commands or scheduling can change endogenous source IDs and source-clock timing. Provider wall time is an intended measured contributor to model latency.

findings.status: Seed pairing does not imply matched operation-level packet shocks
findings.detail: Source messages are assigned the endogenous counter message-N. Packet loss uses (seed, communications, message-N, loss, attempt). Extra or differently ordered queries/orders/telemetry change which physical command receives a given random draw. This is policy-dependent workload, not a direct arm-name draw. The primary packetLoss=0 comparison is unaffected by this draw coupling.
findings.recommendedClaim: Seed-paired exogenous worlds with policy-dependent command-delivery draws; command-level random shocks are not individually matched.
findings.recommendedControl: Preserve the packetLoss=0 contrast. Treat packetLoss=0.05 as a multi-seed robustness analysis, retain all runs and do not attribute a single paired difference entirely to semantic intelligence. If a future study requires matched packet shocks for corresponding commands, preregister an independent exogenous network fault schedule or semantic message identity before measuring; do not retrofit shocks after outcomes.

findings.status: Inspection identity has the same coupling limitation when observationRate is below one
findings.detail: A clarification reply uses (seed, verification, inspection ID, reply). Inspection numbering and command order may differ across policies. Current discovery explicitly sets observationRate=1, so random reply refusal does not distinguish current primary arms. Cohort silentFraction is separate and drawn from stable building IDs, not from inspection counters.

findings.status: Predeclared physical need and authored corpus draws are stable across paired policies
findings.detail: Benchmark place selection, quantity, explicit/contextual style, silence, deadlines, priorities and noise locations/times use stable building or noise-index keys. Authored public signal IDs derive from the stable causeEvent plus family via opaqueId(seed, kind, key), rather than a mutable post counter. Repost and engagement draws for these posts therefore remain keyed to the same public source ID. Controllers may cause additional endogenous reports; the evolving corpus need not remain byte-identical after policy actions.

findings.status: Traffic parameter is a count; congestion and subsequent routing are causally endogenous
findings.detail: traffic=15 means fifteen background vehicles, not fifteen percent. Stable traffic-i IDs and the initial origin draw are matched by seed. Destination draws are keyed to vehicle identity and source-clock time; new targets occur on the same periodic schedule only when that vehicle is idle/arrived. Policy vehicles alter occupancy, waiting and whether a background vehicle is available for its next scheduled trip. Those resulting differences are physical consequences of the policy, not independent exogenous nuisance held constant at each command.
findings.recommendedClaim: Report exact background vehicle count and map extent/fleet, rather than an unsupported traffic percentage. Separate the zero-background control from multi-seed congestion robustness.

findings.status: Narrower network fault model than ordinary source messages
findings.detail: Cross-platform HTTP transport checks actual source connectivity for both organizations and advances the common source clock by networkLatencyMs, capped at the declared horizon. It records each transport delivery/failure. This adapter does not draw source packetLoss and does not model source message bandwidth/congestion for HTTP peer bodies. Ordinary source commands/observations still go through finite source communications and packet-loss logic. Equal use of the adapter in compared linked arms is fair within the implemented model, but does not establish full packet-loss fidelity for federation traffic.
findings.recommendedClaim: Peer transport evidence covers connectivity, nominal latency and recorded HTTP delivery; avoid claiming realistic packet-loss/bandwidth saturation for federation unless a future predeclared model adds those effects.

conclusion: No direct arm/Date.now contamination of physical random seeds was found. The primary zero-loss/zero-background comparison avoids the main command-randomness limitation. Paired seeds match authored exogenous worlds and corpus, not all policy-dependent command shocks or evolving congestion. This audit is source reasoning, not new execution evidence, and makes no benefit, mortality, Gemini or human-performance claim.
